context: Wilde to Frank Harris, [late May 1899], Paris. Back from Switzerland and living on loans. He sends Harris the address of the enameller Armand Point, recommends Mirbeau's Le Jardin des Supplices, asks after Harris's Shakespeare book, and closes by asking for ten pounds.
quote:
From Sebastian Melmoth, Hotel Marsollier, Rue Marsollier, Paris.

My dear Frank, Armand Point’s address is Marlotte, Seine-et-Marne, and if you will send him an impression in wax of your emerald he will be charmed to design and execute a ring for you.

How are you? and how are the automobiles and the Baryes? I no longer, now that you are not here, live in purple and fine linen at Durand’s: such pomp, however, should be intermittent.

If you want to read a terrible little book, order Octave Mirbeau’s ‘Le Jardin des Supplices’: it is quite awful: a Sadique joy in pain pulses in it: it is very revolting to me, but, for all that, wonderful. His soul seems to have wandered in fearsome places. But you, to whom fear is unknown, will face the book with courage. To me it is a sort of grey adder.

How is Shakespeare? He was a mist, and you have made him marble. I wish the Golden Book would appear. Shakespeare: his soul and body.

If you are rolling in gold — and have achieved your victory over Beit and the other lost tribes of Israel, do send me a tenner. Life is rather dust now — and water-wells are rare in the desert. My compliments to Mrs Harris.

Ever Oscar
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 38-40 - one sheet of squared Taverne de l'Opera paper (Societe des Tavernes Pousset & Royale Reunies, 26 Avenue de l'Opera), three sides used: 38 is side 1, 39 the opening of sides 2 and 3, 40 side 4. Heading: 'From Sebastian Melmoth, Hotel Marsollier, Rue Marsollier, Paris' - the fifth appearance of the exile name in this folder, and the volume drops it as it drops the other four. It also explains a discrepancy in our own manifest, which called this the Taverne de l'Opera letter while the volume heads it Hotel Marsollier: the paper is the Taverne's, the address he gives is the hotel's. Both descriptions were right about different things. Emphasis: none across the four sides, a null finding. The title: Mirbeau's book is ‘Le Jardin des Supplices’ in his own inverted commas, not underlined; the volume sets it in italic. Seventh instance of the quotes-to-italic conversion. Null on the French: 'Sadique' is not underlined - the volume's italic is its French convention again Read with care: the strokes that appear to underline 'execute' on side 2 and to overline 'That' are his extended t-crossbars, the same shape that has faked underlines four times already in this pass. Punctuation: his dashes restored; the volume gives commas. 'and how are the automobiles' keeps his lower-case 'and' after the question mark. 1173 - stand, because there the edition read a real difference.
